Round four's mark with the spore drops off. The cap is not untouched, though: dropping the spores made it read as a flag, so the rim is blunter and the underside tucks back under. Overhang is what says mushroom once nothing beneath it is doing the explaining.
A shallower cap, so the top arm sits closer to a true F. Reads as a letter fastest and as a mushroom slowest -- the trade in one picture.
The opposite: a deeper, more arched cap. Unmistakably a fungus, and the F has to work harder to be seen.
The stem swelling into a bag at the base. That bag is the single feature that separates a death cap from a field mushroom, and it is the part almost everyone leaves in the soil.
Gills shown in cross-section under the cap. More information, more to lose when it shrinks.
Thicker stem, shorter ring, tighter counters. Drawn for 29 px rather than scaled down to it -- the usual practice, and worth the extra file.
No cut, no spores, nothing. The silhouette on its own.
With an annulus. The ring is what tells you an Amanita has been there, so it earns its place rather than decorating.
Ring and bag together: a textbook Amanita, which is the shape the whole app is organised around.
Stroked rather than filled. Lighter on a dark ground, and the first to clog at small sizes -- check the 29 before falling for it.
